hints: Apply the binomial theorem to expand $(a - x)^6$ up to the term in $x^3$.
walkthrough:
Expand $(a - x)^6$ in ascending powers of $x$ using the binomial theorem:
$$(a - x)^6 = \binom{6}{0}a^6 + \binom{6}{1}a^5(-x) + \binom{6}{2}a^4(-x)^2 + \binom{6}{3}a^3(-x)^3 + \dots$$

hints: Factorise as a quadratic in $a^2$ and find all exact values of $a$.
walkthrough:
Identify the products that produce an $x^2$ power in $\left(1 + \frac{2}{ax}\right)(a^6 - 6a^5x + 15a^4x^2 - 20a^3x^3 + \dots)$:
$$\text{Terms in } x^2 = [1 \times 15a^4x^2] + \left[\frac{2}{ax} \times (-20a^3x^3)\right] = 15a^4x^2 - 40a^2x^2 = (15a^4 - 40a^2)x^2$$

Equate the combined coefficient to the given value $-20$:
$$15a^4 - 40a^2 = -20 \implies 15a^4 - 40a^2 + 20 = 0 \implies 3a^4 - 8a^2 + 4 = 0$$

Factorise as a quadratic in $a^2$:
$$(a^2 - 2)(3a^2 - 2) = 0$$
$$a^2 = 2 \implies a = \pm\sqrt{2}$$
$$a^2 = \frac{2}{3} \implies a = \pm\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \quad \left(\text{or } \pm\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\right)$$
